title: Agent Infra Leverage
description:
The groundwork the adoption rests on: the machinery that says what a Claude run costs, and the planning that decides what moves and where it goes.

It sits inside the epic rather than ahead of it because neither question is answerable in the abstract. What a context costs is only meaningful against a concrete consumer, and what should move is only decidable once somebody has enumerated what there is — and the consumers are what this epic delivers.

title: Phase 1 - The Swarm Session Boots From the Registry
description:
A swarm session's rules arrive today as one large file every session reads in full, plus a launch prompt written into a shell script. Neither is queryable, neither is measured, and nothing can say which rules a given session is actually bound by. This phase makes that set a composed definition the session is handed, so that changing what a worker knows becomes an edit to a row rather than to a paragraph nobody can measure.

The hazard that shapes the whole phase is that every one of those rules is binding today whether or not anyone can enumerate it. Nothing moves before it has been inventoried and classified, and nothing is deleted from the file it lives in until the replacement has been proven to deliver it — which is why the phase ends with a retirement and a measurement rather than with a mechanism.

title: Aggregator Card — Combined Ride Map
description:
**Given** the /maps cards view with any filter set (view filter, time, routes, partners)
**When** the aggregator card is toggled on
**Then** an always-first card renders the concatenated GPS tracks of ALL filtered rides — one polyline per ride, bounds fitted — like the export map preview, with a stats header (ride count, total distance, photo count) at normal card width; the toggle persists across sessions.

title: Aggregator Card — Photo Aggregation
description:
**Given** the aggregator card is on and the photo feature is enabled
**When** rides are aggregated
**Then** photos discovered in each aggregated ride's time window appear on the aggregator map exactly as on per-ride maps — clustered markers, grid overlay, lightbox — degrading gracefully when the photos proxy or index is absent.

title: Mapping Architect Agent
description: A category-level architect agent for the mapping domain: thin charter stub + registry row + guiding-principles charter, owning the groomed mapping-germane documents (ETL, Strava, photo browser, aggregator surfaces) transferred from Applications Architect, bound to the common instruction band; Applications Architect scope carved down accordingly.

title: Aggregator Card Meta-Pattern
description: The aggregator-card meta-pattern documented as a reusable UI pattern with its two canonical implementations — requirements (SwarmStartCard) and mapping (MapAggregatorCard): always-first placement, persisted toggle in the header row, aggregation source, styling parity with sibling cards, testid conventions.

title: Epic Planning Pattern
description: The planning pattern that generates an epic-based development plan from a requirement, captured as a binding registry instruction bound to every agent, with lineage and rejected variants recorded in memory/agentic-patterns.md. The epic is the container — tracking requirements are retired.

title: Epic Validation & Demo
description: The epic's closure pair. **Given** all implementation features of the epic are built **When** the penultimate validation story has verified them (test cases linked, coverage gaps recorded) **Then** the ultimate capstone story applies the polish pattern across the implemented features and demos the plan on a dev server — the epic is done only when the user has reviewed that demo.

title: Multi-Machine Dev-Server Registry
description: **Given** dev servers run concurrently on more than one machine **When** any session claims, arbitrates, sweeps, or releases a dev_servers row **Then** every mutation is scoped to the acting machine (ports are machine-local), so no machine can delete or kill another machine's live claim.

title: Silent Success — no reassurance notices
description:
**Given** a user-initiated action completes with nothing for the user to decide, repair, or act on
**When** the UI reports back
**Then** it says nothing — the changed state is the confirmation, and a notice appears only when there IS a problem, a choice, or an irreversible consequence.

The instruction-rename alert on the Agents > Instructions page ("Safe: nothing resolves an instruction by name...") is the first application: it fires on success to tell the user that nothing broke, which is noise. It is removed, and the rule is written into the Frontend Architect's owned UI docs so future surfaces inherit it rather than re-deriving it.

title: Phase 2 - The Pipeline Orchestrator Is a Swarm Session
description:
Orchestration runs today only from the session a person happens to be sitting in front of, which ties the one activity that must survive long unattended stretches to a human's window. This phase gives orchestration a session of its own: a generalist with full reach over the coordination surface that plans, reasons, designs and debugs, and that deliberately does none of the maintenance a working session does.

It is the harder test of the definition mechanism, because this consumer is defined as much by what it must not do as by what it may, and a format that can only add capability cannot express that. The question it must surface and must not answer on its own is whether orchestration should eventually happen this way only.

title: Phase 3 - Every AI in Darwin Is a Row
description:
The session a person actually talks to is the last one still carrying its whole rulebook as prose. Moving it onto the same footing as everything else is what makes the roster complete: every AI in the system becomes visible in Darwin, editable there and injectable from there, instead of some being data while the most important one is a file.

It goes last because it is the least recoverable. A worker that boots wrong can be undone and relaunched; the session that would have to notice and do that is the one at risk here. A file kept as a template of last resort is the deliberate answer to that, and deciding what that file must still contain is part of this phase rather than a leftover from it.
